author: Collider
title: Prime Video's 'Every Year After' Sparks Expansion of Carley Fortune's Romance Novels into Major Franchise
text:
The Amazon Prime Video series Every Year After, adapted from Carley Fortune's Every Summer After, has become a global streaming hit. This success has accelerated plans for a second season and a feature film adaptation of Fortune's Meet Me at the Lake, produced by Archewell. The projects share themes of grief, second chances, and lakeside romance, marking the beginning of a broader franchise.
The eight-episode romance series Every Year After , which premiered on Prime Video on June 10, 2026, has quickly become a global streaming hit, consistently ranking either first or second worldwide behind only Off-Campus according to FlixPatrol.
The show, starring Sadie Soverall and Matt Cornett, is adapted from Carley Fortune's 2022 bestselling novel Every Summer After and proves that heartfelt comfort stories can achieve both high viewership and quality. While many viewers were drawn to the charming lake town romance, a significant portion tuned in specifically because of their love for the original book. This success is part of a larger trend: Fortune's work is rapidly expanding into a broader franchise.
Another one of her novels, Meet Me at the Lake (2023), has already been optioned for a feature film by Archewell Productions, the company run by Prince Harry and Meghan The Duchess of Sussex. That project, still in development, is being carefully revised.
Fortune recently discussed the adaptation on the June 18 episode of Open Book With Jenna, where she expressed confidence in the Sussexes, noting they truly understood the core of her story, which she described as a romance that also deeply explores themes of motherhood, grief, and mental health. Meet Me at the Lake follows a more mature romance centering on Fern Brookbanks and Will Baxter.
Their connection begins with a unforgettable date in their twenties, but a failed reunion pact and nine years of separation pass before Will reappears in Fern's life as she inherits and runs her late mother's lakeside resort. The novel shares clear thematic DNA with Every Summer After an idyllic lakeside setting, a bond that spans years, unresolved grief, and a second-chance romance built on rebuilding trust.
With Season 2 of Every Year After already confirmed this season will shift focus to Charlie (Michael Bradway) and adapt Fortune's 2025 sequel One Golden Summer the author's novels are solidifying their place as a growing television and film franchise. Fans can now look forward to multiple on-screen adaptations of Fortune's work, all centered around emotional, location-driven romances that resonate across different age groups
